title: Kähler comparison of the real and Dolbeault Laplacians
statement: All vector spaces below are over the complex field $\mathbf C$ [def-weil-field]. Let $M$ be a complex manifold without boundary of complex dimension $n\geq0$, equipped with a Kähler metric: a smooth positive definite Hermitian metric whose associated real $(1,1)$-form is closed. Let $A^k(M;\mathbf C)$ be smooth complex differential forms of total degree $k$, let $A^{p,q}(M)$ be their type subspaces, and let $d=\partial+\bar\partial$ be the exterior derivative. Let $d^*$ and $\bar\partial^*$ be the formal adjoints for the metric volume and pointwise Hermitian inner products (characterized by integration against compactly supported smooth test forms). Define $\Delta_d=dd^*+d^*d$ and $\Delta_{\bar\partial}=\bar\partial\bar\partial^*+\bar\partial^*\bar\partial$. On smooth complex differential forms one has the identity $$\Delta_d=2\Delta_{\bar\partial}.$$ No compactness assumption is needed for this identity of differential operators.

source.place: WANTED locally: Wenrui Kong, Notes on Complex Geometry (April 9, 2025), §6.4, Proposition 6.12, printed p.26; read online https://cims.nyu.edu/~wk805/files/Complex_Geometry_Notes.pdf. The Laplacian equality in the Kähler identities.

proof.text: Put $A=\partial$ and $B=\bar\partial$, acting on the direct sum of all total degrees. The differential relations in [lem-sfb-dolbeault-acyclic-resolution] give $A^2=B^2=AB+BA=0$. Only these stated relations are used, not resolution exactness or acyclicity. They can be applied on holomorphic coordinate domains, which are Hausdorff and second countable, and then hold globally because equality of smooth forms is local. Put $A^*=\partial^*$, $B^*=\bar\partial^*$ and $\Delta_A=AA^*+A^*A$, $\Delta_B=BB^*+B^*B$. The defining formal-adjoint relation gives $d^*=A^*+B^*$: for compactly supported test forms $u,v$, expand $\langle(A+B)u,v\rangle_{L^2}$ and move $A$ and $B$ separately to the other entry. This identifies the adjoint uniquely: if the difference $T$ of two proposed adjoints paired to zero with every test $u$, choose $u=\chi Tv$ with $\chi\geq0$ supported in a chart to obtain $\int\chi|Tv|^2=0$, forcing $Tv=0$ there. The same compact-support test gives the pointwise identity for arbitrary smooth $v$.

source.place: §3.1, Theorem 3.4 (type differentials); §6.1 formal adjoints; explicit adjoint-sum argument by Q58

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-kahler-first-order-commutators] with the given metric, with $L=\omega\wedge(-)$ and $Q=\Lambda=L^*$. Its hypotheses are exactly the complex manifold, positive Hermitian metric and closed associated form in the statement. With $[P,R]=PR-RP$, its two formulas read $[Q,A]=iB^*$ and $[Q,B]=-iA^*$, equivalently $B^*=-i(QA-AQ)$ and $A^*=i(QB-BQ)$. The adjoints here are the same formal adjoints used in step 1, defined with the same metric and volume.

source.place: §6.4, Definition 6.10, Lemma 6.11, Proposition 6.12, first-order commutator lines

proof.text: The mixed terms vanish by direct expansion, using the differential relations of [lem-sfb-dolbeault-acyclic-resolution] and the substitutions from [lem-sfb-kahler-first-order-commutators]: $$AB^*+B^*A=-i(AQA-A^2Q+QA^2-AQA)=0,$$ $$BA^*+A^*B=i(BQB-B^2Q+QB^2-BQB)=0.$$ Products mean composition, so these cancellations use associativity and distributivity, not an interchange of noncommuting factors.

source.place: §6.4, Proposition 6.12, Laplacian line; explicit mixed-term expansion by Q58

proof.text: The same substitutions give $$\Delta_A=i(AQB-ABQ+QBA-BQA),$$ $$\Delta_B=-i(BQA-BAQ+QAB-AQB).$$ Therefore $$\Delta_A-\Delta_B=i\bigl(Q(AB+BA)-(AB+BA)Q\bigr)=0,$$ by $AB+BA=0$ from [lem-sfb-dolbeault-acyclic-resolution]. These expansions use precisely the two first-order identities in [lem-sfb-kahler-first-order-commutators]; thus $\Delta_A=\Delta_B$.

source.place: §6.4, Proposition 6.12, Laplacian line; explicit diagonal-term expansion by Q58

proof.text: Finally expand $d=A+B$ and $d^*=A^*+B^*$: $$\Delta_d=\Delta_A+\Delta_B+(AB^*+B^*A)+(BA^*+A^*B)=2\Delta_B=2\Delta_{\bar\partial}.$$ The mixed terms vanish by step 3 and the diagonal terms agree by step 4. Every identity acts on arbitrary smooth forms and every adjoint is formal, so no global integrability, compactness, completeness, or boundary condition has entered. With zero spaces outside the allowed degrees the calculation also includes the top and bottom degrees, dimension zero and the empty manifold.

source.place: §6.4, Proposition 6.12, Laplacian line; explicit final expansion by Q58
